_comment: Permission settings for the UNATTENDED Sunday devlog cron run only.
Not used by interactive sessions.
WHY: the cron runs Claude headless, and its inputs include git commit
messages. Today that is safe because there is one committer. It stops
being safe the moment outside contributions land, which is a stated goal
of build-plan.md -- a commit message is attacker-controlled text, and it
would be flowing into an agent that can write files unsupervised.
THE PRIMARY CONTROL IS NOT THIS FILE. It is the allow-list in
devlog-cron.sh: Edit/Write are granted only for ./devlog/**, and
--permission-mode acceptEdits is deliberately not used. Everything below
is defence in depth.
That ordering was learned the hard way. The first version of this fix
relied on the deny list below plus acceptEdits and unscoped 'Write,Edit'
in --allowedTools. A test write to $HOME SUCCEEDED: the deny list
enumerates repo paths, and the escape was outside the repo entirely. A
deny-list cannot contain a tool that was granted for every path.
SYNTAX WARNING, verified empirically 2026-08-25: a Write(path) DENY rule
is SILENTLY IGNORED by file permission checks. Only Edit(path) rules
apply, and they cover every file-editing tool including Write. A deny
list written with Write(...) looks like a control and is not one.
Do NOT add a catch-all like Edit(./*) -- also tested: it matches the
project directory itself and denies everything, including devlog, which
would silently break the Sunday draft rather than failing loudly.
Verified end to end 2026-08-25 against the real repo: devlog/ writes
succeed; src/ is denied via relative AND absolute path; $HOME is refused;
.git/hooks is refused by the harness's own sensitive-file guard.
LIMITATION: the repo section is an enumeration, so a NEW top-level file
or directory is not denied here until it is added. The allow-list in
devlog-cron.sh is what actually bounds this, and it does not enumerate.
